battle.name: 巴比倫-埃什南納-馬里戰爭
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞南部兩河下游
battle.brief: 公元前1762年，巴比倫王辛姆里-里姆與埃什南納王伊普庫努姆、馬里王伊什-達干在兩河下游開戰。聯軍東進，在烏爾姆河畔擊潰王軍，辛姆里-里姆棄城西逃亞述。銅矛手在兩軍的密集矛陣裡頂住了最初的衝鋒，決定戰局的卻是河患與兵糧。巴比倫的崩解與阿摩利特王國的交接，由這一戰開始。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前十八世紀末兩河下游三個城邦聯盟體系正面碰撞的結果。巴比倫一方是阿摩利特人第一王朝：漢謨拉比在位期間（前1792–前1750年）以王權、阿姆巴神的司法、灌溉運河與受控的征役隊建立起以水利為骨架的帝國，其子辛姆里-里姆於前1772年繼位。埃什南納（Tell Asmar，楔形文字作 Ešnunna，漢謨拉比法典序言中稱「馬爾吉姆」）立在底格里斯河東岸的高地，距巴比倫僅約一百五十公里，扼住東北方通往亞述、扎格羅斯山脈與埃梅特高原的商路。馬里（Tell Hariri）位在幼發拉底中游偏下，靠一整套人工運河與水門維持城市，是阿摩利特諸國中最善於用水利作武器者。埃什南納與馬里結盟並非偶然：兩者都靠幼發拉底與底格里斯的水源與貨物流通為生，一旦巴比倫的運河政策改變了水的分配與航運，這兩國的腹背就同時受威脅。亞述當時處於中亞述時期，刻意與巴比倫保持距離，卻是流亡者最後的收容所。三方的指揮系統都很簡陋：國王居中，地方首領與軍官分掌兵眾，命令靠縱隊內的口信與旗幟傳遞，縱隊一旦拉開便難以協調。
countriesEn: This war was the outcome of a head-on collision between three city-state alliance systems in the lower two rivers in the late eighteenth century BC. On the Babylonian side stood the first dynasty of the Amorites: during the reign of Hammurabi (1792 to 1750 BC) an empire was built on royal authority, the justice of the god Shamash, irrigation canals and a controlled levy, an empire whose skeleton was hydraulic, and his son Zimri-Lim succeeded him in 1772 BC. Eshnunna (Tell Asmar, written in cuneiform as Ešnunna and called Malgium in the prologue of the Code of Hammurabi) stood on the high ground east of the Tigris, only about a hundred and fifty kilometres from Babylon, and held the trade routes leading north-east toward Assyria, the Zagros mountains and the Emmet plateau. Mari (Tell Hariri) lay on the lower middle Euphrates and kept its city alive with a whole system of artificial canals and water gates; it was the most accomplished among the Amorite states in using waterworks as a weapon. That Eshnunna and Mari should ally was no accident: both lived on the water and the flow of goods of the Euphrates and the Tigris, and once the canal policy of Babylon altered the distribution of water and the pattern of navigation, the backs of both were exposed at once. Assyria at that moment stood in the Middle Assyrian period and deliberately kept its distance from Babylon, yet it was the haven that finally took in the exile. The command structures of all three were crude: the king in the middle, local dynasts and officers holding the troops, orders carried by word of mouth and by standards inside the column, so that once the column drew apart, coordination became difficult.
people: 辛姆里-里姆是這場戰爭裡敗方的主角。巴比倫王表A記他共在位十一年，年代為前1772年至前1761年，而前1762年正是他在位第十一年，也就是烏爾姆河一役之年。他的父親漢謨拉比在《法典》序言裡自稱是「饒過馬爾吉姆人民的人」，而辛姆里-里姆一朝的宮廷書簡則顯示，國王對埃什南納仍抱有相當的倚重。埃什南納方面有兩位王：先與巴比倫結盟、後與之反目的雅烏西姆，他的書簡（如 VAS 16 195）向漢謨拉比預警伊普庫努姆的敵意；真正舉兵東進的是伊普庫努姆。馬里王伊什-達干是聯軍的實際統帥，戰後把自己的長子亞斯瑪-阿杜送到巴比倫即位（前1761–前1750年在位），自己也在前1750年登上巴比倫王位，最終在赫梯王穆爾西里一世兵臨城下時國破家亡。辛姆里-里姆西逃亞述，在那裡得到亞述王的收留，最終死於亞述，死因有不同說法。除王侯之外，決定戰局的是一批沒有留下姓名的群體：巴比倫的城防軍與征發農兵、馬里的弓手與車隊、埃什南納的工匠與譯員，以及馬里王宮裡那批把每日糧秣、徵役與外交都寫下來的書吏。
peopleEn: Zimri-Lim is the central figure of the losing side in this war. Babylonian King List A gives him eleven years, from 1772 to 1761 BC, and 1762 BC is precisely the eleventh year of his reign, the year of the battle at the Ulm. His father Hammurabi calls himself in the prologue of the Code the one who spared the people of Malgium, while the court correspondence of Zimri-Lim's own reign shows that the king still placed considerable reliance on Eshnunna. Eshnunna had two kings in this story: Yawsim, first an ally of Babylon and later its enemy, whose letter (such as VAS 16 195) warned Hammurabi of Ipkunum's hostility; and Ipkunum himself, the one who actually marched east. Ishi-Dagan, king of Mari, was the operational commander of the coalition; after the war he sent his elder son Yasmah-Addu to take the throne of Babylon (1761 to 1750 BC) and himself ascended that throne in 1750 BC, only to lose kingdom and city when the Hittite king Mursili I came down on him. Zimri-Lim fled west into Assyria, was received by the Assyrian king, and died there; the manner of his death is variously reported. Besides the kings and princes, what decided the battle was a host of people who left no names: the garrison and the levied farmers of Babylon, the archers and the chariot crews of Mari, the craftsmen and the interpreters of Eshnunna, and the scribes of the Mari palace who wrote down the daily grain, the levies and the diplomacy.
kits: 卡面上這件埃及長矛，屬於青銅時代最基本也最耐用的直刃矛：青銅矛頭以榫口或縛紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩。它同時是兩河流域步兵的標準配備——第四千紀的蘇美爾與阿卡德軍隊所用的正是同一類青銅矛，烏爾的《標準圖》與納拉姆辛石碑上的持矛步兵、銅斧與圓盾，把這種武器的樣子保存至今。辛姆里-里姆時代的巴比倫步兵以密集成排的矛兵為核心，矛尖朝前抵住來敵，後排再以弓手覆蓋。巴比倫的弓是長達兩公尺的複合弓，竹木為身、角與皮條為飾，箭鏃用銅或骨；盾以柳條為框、外蒙獸皮，重要部隊另加銅皮。鎧甲方面，蘇美爾末期留下的成組銅鱗甲與頭盔說明重裝步兵確實存在，但因銅料昂貴，多數人只有盾與頭盔。馬里與埃什南納的守城器械包括壕溝、水門、夯土與燒磚城牆，攻城時則用斜坡與撞槌。運輸靠驢、騾、牛車與河運；馬里王宮檔案中的「口糧」卷宗記錄按人頭發放穀物，是已知最早的成文後勤制度之一。銅是這支軍隊真正的瓶頸：銅來自安納托利亞山區與迪姆蘭，馬里書簡裡留有自迪姆蘭運銅的清單，銅料的遲滯直接決定了矛兵能配到多少銅矛，也讓這場衝突不只是一場疆土之爭，更是兩河上游對金屬資源的爭奪。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is the plainest and most durable thrusting weapon of the Bronze Age: a bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder. It was at the same time the standard arm of Mesopotamian infantry, for the Sumerian and Akkadian armies of the fourth millennium used exactly this class of bronze spear, and the Standard of Ur and the stele of Naram-Sin preserve the look of the weapon in the hands of spearmen, bronze axes and round shields. The Babylonian infantry of Zimri-Lim's day was built on dense ranks of spearmen, points forward against the oncoming enemy, with archers covering them from behind. The Babylonian bow was a composite bow about two metres long, of bamboo and wood with horn and hide bindings, its arrowheads of copper or bone; shields were wicker frames covered with hide, and important units added a facing of copper. As for armour, the sets of copper scale armour and helmets left by the end of the Sumerian period show that heavy infantry did exist, but since copper was dear, most men had only shield and helmet. The siege equipment of Mari and Eshnunna included ditches, water gates, rammed earth and fired-brick walls, and the assault used ramps and battering rams. Transport rested on donkeys, mules, ox carts and river traffic; the ration tablets of the Mari palace archive record the issue of grain by head, one of the earliest written logistics systems known. Copper was the real bottleneck of these armies: it came from the Anatolian highlands and from Dilmun, and the Mari letters preserve lists of copper shipped from Dilmun, so the sluggishness of the copper supply decided how many bronze-tipped spears a formation could be issued, and made this conflict not only a contest for territory but a contest for the metal resources of the upper rivers.
tactics: 兩河流域此時的野戰沒有留下可靠的陣圖，但可以從同期馬里書簡與漢謨拉比時代的相關記載拼出輪廓。編制上，一支野戰軍通常分三段：前鋒是以弓手為主的散兵，負責騷擾與遮蔽；本隊是密集的矛兵與重裝步兵，兩翼配雙輪或四輪輕戰車，車上三人，一人射箭、一人持矛、一人駕馭；殿後由步騎混編，負責掩護糧車與撤退。進攻時先以弓手齊射削弱敵陣，再由矛兵頂住反衝，車隊從缺口突入縱深，不求殲滅而求把敵人驅散於平原之上，因阿摩利特的戰爭多在城郊開闊地進行，擊潰即算成功，攻城另作長期工程。守城方倚靠城牆、壕溝與水門消耗攻方，攻方必須填壕、架斜坡，然後以撞槌破門。河道是這一戰的關鍵：聯軍沿底格里斯河與支渠推進，糧車與車隊只能沿堤行進，一旦遇洪或道路潰陷，縱隊就會斷成數段，士氣與指揮都隨之中斷。辛姆里-里姆的巴比倫軍隊在烏爾姆河一線迎擊，其部署把城防軍與征發農兵混編，後方臨近巴比倫城，士氣與退路兼顧，卻在洪患與地形夾擊下被聯軍切斷。
tacticsEn: No reliable diagram of a field battle from Mesopotamia of this age survives, but the outline can be pieced together from the Mari correspondence and from what is recorded of the age of Hammurabi. In organisation, a field army was usually in three parts: a vanguard of loose skirmishers, chiefly archers, responsible for harassment and screening; the main body, dense spearmen and heavy infantry, with light two-wheeled or four-wheeled chariots on the flanks, each chariot carrying three men, one shooting, one holding a spear and one driving; and a rear guard of mixed foot and horse covering the baggage trains and the retreat. On the attack the archers first volleyed to weaken the opposing line, the spearmen then bore the counter-charge, and the chariots drove into the gap and into the depth of the enemy, seeking not annihilation but the scattering of the enemy across the open, because Amorite wars were fought on the open ground outside the towns, where breaking the enemy counted as victory and the siege was left as a separate and long engineering task. The defenders relied on walls, ditches and water gates to wear the attackers down, while the attackers had to fill the ditch, build the ramp and then break the gate with a ram. The river was the key of this particular war: the coalition advanced along the Tigris and its canals, and the baggage carts and chariots could only travel on the levees; once a flood came or a road gave way, the column broke into several segments, and morale and command broke with it. Zimri-Lim's Babylonian army met the attack on the line of the Ulm; its deployment mixed garrison troops with levied farmers, keeping the city of Babylon close behind so that morale and the line of retreat were both covered, yet it was cut apart by the coalition between flood and terrain.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：漢謨拉比在位前1792–前1750年；辛姆里-里姆前1772–前1761年，巴比倫王表A記其十一年，前1762年為其在位第十一年；亞斯瑪-阿杜前1761–前1750年共十六年；伊什-達干前1750–前1759或前1758年在位兩年；其後的阿卜迪-米爾庫提在位僅三個月，赫梯王穆爾西里一世即洗劫巴比倫 —— 通行中年代定於前1759或前1758年，而本站採用嘅中文參考資料另有一套定年，繫於前1595年（同池《巴比倫的洗劫》一卡即用後者），本篇兩種說法並列，唔取其一。第二類是距離與地理：巴比倫至埃什南納約一百五十公里，至馬里約三百四十公里，至底格里斯河最近渡口約一百公里；埃什南納距底格里斯東岸約二十公里；巴比倫城牆圈出的舊城約近百公頃。戰場所在嘅烏爾姆河本身無從考定，有底格里斯支流、國王運河等不同說法，故本場經緯度只能按底格里斯下游一線作大致標定。第三類是物證與文獻量：馬里王宮檔案出土泥板逾兩萬件，其中書簡佔一萬五千件左右，年代橫跨前1770至前1750年，數量之大足以支撐逐日後勤的重建；埃什南納的方形神廟出土一批彩繪石膏崇拜者雕像，年代在早王朝至古巴比倫時期，可見該城神廟經濟的規模。至於交戰雙方的兵員，本時代的阿摩利特王權有「傾國之兵」的修辭傳統，卻無可核實的數字，合理的量級是數千至數萬，任何具體傷亡數字都屬臆測。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: Hammurabi reigned 1792 to 1750 BC; Zimri-Lim reigned 1772 to 1761 BC, and Babylonian King List A gives him eleven years, so that 1762 BC is the eleventh year of his reign; Yasmah-Addu reigned 1761 to 1750 BC, sixteen years; Ishi-Dagan reigned two years, 1750 to 1759 or 1758 BC; Abdi-Milkuti then held the throne for three months only, and the Hittite king Mursili I sacked Babylon in 1759 or 1758 BC. The second class is distance and geography: about a hundred and fifty kilometres from Babylon to Eshnunna, about three hundred and forty to Mari, about a hundred to the nearest crossing of the Tigris; Eshnunna stands about twenty kilometres from the east bank of the Tigris; the old city enclosed by the walls of Babylon covers close to a hundred hectares. The third class is the material and the bulk of the documentation: the palace archive of Mari has yielded more than twenty thousand tablets, of which about fifteen thousand are letters, spanning roughly 1770 to 1750 BC, a quantity large enough to allow the logistics of individual days to be reconstructed; the Square Temple at Eshnunna has produced a set of painted gypsum statues of worshippers dating from the Early Dynastic to the Old Babylonian period, which shows the scale of that city's temple economy. As for the numbers of men on both sides, the Amorite kingship of this age had a tradition of rhetoric about the whole land's forces, but no verifiable figure survives; the reasonable order of magnitude is thousands to tens of thousands, and any specific figure for losses is conjecture.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。最外一層是灌溉經濟的分配：巴比倫在漢謨拉比時代開鑿運河，把水與鹽從幼發拉底引向北，運河沿線的收益與航運的方便讓巴比倫越過了傳統的城邦邊界，而埃什南納與馬里正是被改道的水與貨源的主人。第二層是阿摩利特王國之間的聯盟政治：漢謨拉比一生以聯盟與分化的手法對付埃什南納，這種以友誼換服從的體制在父子交接時最容易崩壞；馬里王宮書簡裡保存的雅烏西姆致漢謨拉比的警告信，說明到前1770年代，埃什南納內部已在策劃反噬巴比倫。第三層是王位繼承的脆弱：辛姆里-里姆繼承的是一個靠水利與司法維繫、而非靠野戰連勝維持的政權，軍隊的戰鬥力取決於能否把城防軍、農兵與雇傭兵捏合起來。第四層是直接導火線：前1762年，埃什南納王伊普庫努姆與馬里王伊什-達干以西聯軍的姿態大舉東進，兩國的距離足以在巴比倫得到消息之前就已逼近，聯軍選擇在巴比倫西側的烏爾姆河一線迎戰，而辛姆里-里姆選擇出城迎敵，不願把戰場與糧道一同交給對手。
causeEn: There are four layers to the outbreak. The outermost is the distribution of an irrigated economy: in the age of Hammurabi, Babylon cut canals, drawing water and salt north from the Euphrates, and the revenue along those canals and the convenience of the navigation carried Babylon across the old boundaries of the city states, while Eshnunna and Mari were precisely the owners of the water and the freight whose course had been turned aside. The second layer is alliance politics among the Amorite kingdoms: Hammurabi spent his life handling Eshnunna by alliance and division, and such a system, which buys obedience with friendship, is most likely to break at a handover from father to son; the letter of Yawsim to Hammurabi preserved in the Mari palace archive shows that by the 1770s BC the court of Eshnunna was already planning to turn on Babylon. The third layer is the fragility of the succession: Zimri-Lim inherited a state held together by hydraulics and justice rather than by a run of victories in the field, and the fighting power of his army depended on whether the garrison, the farmers and the mercenaries could be welded into one force. The fourth layer is the immediate occasion: in 1762 BC the king of Eshnunna, Ipkunum, and the king of Mari, Ishi-Dagan, advanced east in a posture that announced a coalition war, and the distance between their two cities was short enough for the armies to close before Babylon had properly heard of it; the coalition chose to meet the attack on the line of the Ulm west of Babylon, while Zimri-Lim chose to leave the city and meet them in the open, unwilling to hand over both the field and the supply road to the enemy.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，比戰役本身更重要。第一，巴比倫第一王朝實際終結。辛姆里-里姆西逃亞述並死於異鄉，巴比倫王位落入馬里王伊什-達干與其子亞斯瑪-阿杜之手，前1750年伊什-達干自稱王，赫梯王穆爾西里一世隨即洗劫巴比倫（通行中年代繫於前1759或前1758年，中文參考資料另繫於前1595年），馬里系的王國連同其宮廷一起崩潰，亞斯瑪-阿杜本人下落不明。第二，阿摩利特世界的重心整體北移與東移：巴比倫從兩河的核心變成被掠奪的對象，海陸兩大阿摩利特王國（馬里、埃什南納、亞述）成為主角，中巴比倫時期（喀什特的加西特諸國）填補了帝國崩解後的空白，直到亞述新帝國時代巴比倫才重新成為強權。第三，阿卡德文明圈因此擴張到安納托利亞：赫梯人帶走的巴比倫工匠與泥板，讓阿卡德語成為安納托利亞宮廷的書寫語言，也把巴比倫的法律與天文傳統帶過山去。第四，銅與帝國的關係被這場衝突徹底攤開：巴比倫既失去對銅源的組織能力，也失去在戰場上使用銅兵的能力，銅矛作為步兵骨幹的時代由此走向尾聲。
impactEn: The consequences of this war matter more than the battle itself. First, the first Babylonian dynasty effectively ended. Zimri-Lim fled west to Assyria and died in exile, the throne of Babylon passed to the Mari king Ishi-Dagan and his son Yasmah-Addu, Ishi-Dagan took the title of king himself in 1750 BC, and in 1759 or 1758 BC the Hittite king Mursili I sacked Babylon, so that the Mari dynasty collapsed together with its court and Yasmah-Addu himself was never accounted for. Second, the centre of gravity of the Amorite world shifted north and east: Babylon changed from the core of the two rivers into something to be plundered, while the two great Amorite kingdoms of the sea and the land, Mari, Eshnunna and Assyria, became the actors of the age, and the Middle Babylonian period, with the Kassite states of Babylonia, filled the gap left by the collapse of the empire; Babylon did not become a great power again until the age of the Neo-Assyrian empire. Third, the Akkadian sphere of civilisation was thereby extended into Anatolia: the craftsmen and the tablets that the Hittites carried away from Babylon made Akkadian the written language of the Anatolian court and carried Babylonian law and astronomy over the mountains. Fourth, the connection between copper and empire was laid bare by this conflict: Babylon lost both the organisation of its copper supply and the ability to fight with copper-tipped arms, and the age of the bronze spear as the backbone of infantry was thereby brought to its close.
result: 就戰役本身而言，結果是明確的：聯軍在烏爾姆河一役擊潰巴比倫王軍，辛姆里-里姆一方沒有換回任何土地，國王本人西逃亞述，於前1761年死於那裡；巴比倫王位隨即由馬里系的伊什-達干與亞斯瑪-阿杜接管。但勝負的機制並不簡單。聯軍之所以能在開闊地壓倒巴比倫，靠的是三重優勢：埃什南納與馬里之間成熟的陸路聯繫，與馬里自身的河運及糧秣體系；阿摩利特城邦之間長期流傳的商路知識，使聯軍熟悉底格里斯與幼發拉底的渡口與支渠；以及巴比倫軍隊在城郊多綁於城防與灌溉利益，一離開熟悉的渠網便失去戰術主動。洪水與河岸泥灘則把巴比倫縱隊的機動優勢抹去，讓車隊與糧車堵成一團。結果的指向因此很清楚：這不是一場可以靠外交復原的敗仗，而是舊巴比倫帝國結構的終結訊號。此後的十五年裡，馬里系的兩位王在巴比倫與馬里之間來回經營，赫梯人帶著刀兵進入巴比倫（通行中年代繫於前1759或前1758年，中文參考資料另繫於前1595年），連同城中的神像一起帶走，兩河下游重回城邦林立的局面，長達三百年的中巴比倫時期由此開始。
resultEn: As to the battle itself, the outcome is plain: the coalition broke Zimri-Lim's army at the Ulm, the Babylonians recovered no ground at all, the king himself fled west into Assyria and died there in 1761 BC, and the throne of Babylon passed at once to the Mari dynasty of Ishi-Dagan and Yasmah-Addu. But the mechanism of the victory is not a simple one. What allowed the coalition to overwhelm the Babylonians on open ground was a threefold advantage: the settled overland connection between Eshnunna and Mari together with Mari's own river traffic and grain system; the knowledge of the trade routes long passed between Amorite cities, which made the coalition familiar with the fords and side canals of the Tigris and the Euphrates; and the fact that the Babylonian army, tethered at home to the city's defence and to the irrigation interests, lost its tactical initiative as soon as it left the network of channels it knew. Flood and river mud then cancelled the mobility of the Babylonian column, jamming the wagons and the baggage train together. The direction of the result is therefore clear: this was not a defeat that diplomacy could repair, but the signal of the end of the structure of the Old Babylonian empire. During the fifteen years that followed, the two Mari kings worked back and forth between Babylon and Mari, until in 1759 or 1758 BC the Hittites came into Babylon with their arms and carried away the gods of the city with them; the lower two rivers fell back into a landscape of separate city states, and the Middle Babylonian period of some three centuries began.
